slides.title: Copying explains the collective behavior of AI agents in the wild
slides.tldr: COPYING DRIVES COLLECTIVE AI AGENT BEHAVIOR
slides.highlight: This research demonstrates how simple copying mechanisms can produce complex collective structures and conventions among AI agents, providing insights for the societal-scale simulation of hybrid human-AI societies in MIMIC.

card.one_liner: AI agents' collective behavior in the wild is primarily driven by proportional copying of recent environment exposure.
card.key_idea: Three minimal models show agents choose pages, usernames, and phrasing by copying options in proportion to their visibility in the recent feed or current page.
card.evaluation: Analyzed 13,661 edits from 1,201 agents on a public wiki; models reproduced heavy-tailed page distributions, name frequencies, and convention patchworks.
card.limitation: The study relies on reconstructed visibility (exposure) rather than logged attention, as agents' actual reading logs were unavailable.

slides.title: HiBRIDGE: A Hierarchical Bayesian Neural Network Framework for Interpretable Dialogue Management in Group-Robot Interaction
slides.tldr: INTERPRETABLE DIALOGUE MANAGEMENT FOR GROUP-ROBOT INTERACTION
slides.highlight: HiBRIDGE uses a hierarchical Bayesian neural network to manage group-robot dialogue, offering uncertainty-aware predictions and more interpretable explanations of robot behavior. This is relevant to RwB's focus on human-robot interaction and embodied social robots.

card.one_liner: HiBRIDGE is a hierarchical Bayesian framework for interpretable dialogue management in group-robot interactions.
card.key_idea: It uses a hierarchical Bayesian neural network to decompose behavior selection into structured stages (e.g., initiative vs. responsive), employing decision-tree surrogates to generate interpretable explanations.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on three offline HRI datasets, an online study (N=20), and an in-person study (N=12). Bayesian models outperformed deterministic and state-of-the-art baselines.

slides.title: SocioGesture: Real-Time and Adaptive Social Gesture Perception for Human-Robot Interaction
slides.highlight: This work introduces a low-latency system for recognizing social cues like invitations and refusals, which is relevant to RwB's focus on human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: SocioGesture is a real-time, adaptive social gesture perception system for robust human-robot interaction.
card.key_idea: A lightweight dual-stream body-hand model using confidence-aware skeleton encoding, occlusion-aware training, and an uncertainty-driven offline adaptation loop for vocabulary expansion.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via LOSO cross-validation on a custom HRI dataset and live Unitree G1 deployment; showed high robustness to joint occlusion and real-time edge latency.
card.limitation: Cannot recover information from severe occlusions and relies on offline labeling, limiting the speed of learning from large interaction datasets.

slides.title: Establishing a Dynamic Multimodal HRI Dataset for Engagement Analysis with a Humanoid Robot
slides.highlight: This work proposes a data-collection protocol integrating physiological signals and behavioral data to analyze user engagement with humanoid robots, supporting RwB's focus on human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: Proposed experimental design for a multimodal HRI dataset to analyze user engagement via physiological and behavioral signals.
card.key_idea: A synchronized data-collection protocol integrating wearable physiological signals (EDA, PPG), IMU motion data, robot kinematics, and 3D/RGB-D vision across three levels of collaborative task complexity.
card.evaluation: Not clearly stated; the paper describes a proposed experimental design and protocol rather than reporting results from a completed study.
card.limitation: The study is currently a conceptual design; data collection and implementation are listed as future work.

slides.title: Realbotix Testing Humanoid Robots at Live Events
slides.highlight: Realbotix is testing humanoid robots for crowd presentations, which is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

slides.title: ConversationalVoice: Full-Duplex Speech Data from Real Conversations through Source-Faithful Reconstruction and Conversation-Grounded Expansion
slides.highlight: This work introduces a pipeline to reconstruct and expand real-world two-speaker conversations, preserving turn-taking, overlaps, and backchannel behavior. It is relevant to HyECHO's focus on diarization and listener modeling within hybrid human-AI team states.

card.one_liner: ConversationalVoice transforms real two-speaker audio into separated, reconstructed, and expanded full-duplex speech training data.
card.key_idea: A three-stage pipeline: separation recovers original tracks; reconstruction regenerates clean speech with explicit timing/tags; expansion generates new, context-grounded dialogue following observed interaction patterns.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via NISQA, DNSMOS, WER, and Gemini-based judgments. Results show high speaker similarity (0.983-0.991) and strong contextual coherence (4.94/5).
card.limitation: Evaluation is entirely automatic; downstream gains in full-duplex model training were not measured.

slides.title: Predictive-Coding-Based Autonomous Regulation of Internally Generated and Externally Coupled Processing in Human-Robot Interaction
slides.highlight: This research proposes a mechanism using a predictive-coding-inspired variational recurrent neural network to balance internal predictions and sensory input during physical human-robot interaction. It is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: A mechanism for humanoid robots to autonomously balance internal predictions and sensory input during physical interaction.
card.key_idea: A PV-RNN uses accumulated reconstruction error as an endogenous signal to switch between high-meta-prior (internal) and low-meta-prior (sensory-coupled) processing regimes online.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on a Torobo humanoid robot across three physical interaction tasks; results showed reduced reconstruction error, prospective prediction error, and physical conflict.
card.limitation: The regulatory policy and hyperparameters are predefined and calibrated manually rather than being learned autonomously from data.

slides.title: Social Intuition vs. Machine Reasoning: Anticipating Human-Robot Interaction from multiple modalities
slides.tldr: BENCHMARKING HUMAN VS. MACHINE INTERACTION PREDICTION
slides.highlight: This research evaluates the ability of vision-language and pose-based models to predict human intention to interact, highlighting the gap between machine reasoning and human social intuition. It is relevant to RwB's focus on human-robot interaction and embodied social robots.

card.one_liner: Humans significantly outperform vision-language models in anticipating human-robot interactions using egocentric video and social cues.
card.key_idea: Benchmarking human intuition against lightweight pose-based models (LSTM, ST-GCN, SkateFormer) and various VLMs using different modalities (pose, image crops, and egocentric video) to predict interaction intent.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on 100 HUI360 test tracks using F1-score. Results show humans outperform VLMs, and model size does not correlate with better performance.
card.limitation: VLMs struggle to reason simultaneously about temporal, spatial, and social cues, often reducing the task to simple approach detection.

slides.title: Noise Adaptive Streaming Audio-Visual Speech Token Enhancement for Robust Full-Duplex Spoken Dialogue Models
slides.tldr: AUDIO-VISUAL SPEECH TOKEN ENHANCEMENT FOR FULL-DUPLEX DIALOGUE
slides.highlight: AV-STE uses lip video and noisy audio to restore semantic speech tokens, improving response coherence in full-duplex systems. This supports HyECHO's goals of multimodal social perception and robust listener modeling in hybrid human-AI teams.

card.one_liner: AV-STE enhances corrupted semantic speech tokens using lip video to improve noisy full-duplex dialogue robustness.
card.key_idea: A modular streaming front-end using a causal AV-HuBERT encoder and noise-adaptive fusion (cross-attention and entropy-based modulation) to restore semantic tokens for a frozen speech LLM.
card.evaluation: Tested on LRS3 and Seamless Interaction using token accuracy and GPT-4o coherence scores. Results show significant gains under severe noise (-10dB) and speaker interference.
card.limitation: Sensitive to domain shift and assumes reliable visual input; robustness to visual occlusion or missing video remains unexplored.

slides.title: KABURI-TTS: Phoneme-Keyed Activity-conditioned Bi-channel Utterance Rendering for Interaction
slides.highlight: KABURI-TTS enables the generation of human-like overlaps and turn-taking in bi-channel spoken dialogue, supporting the modeling of interaction states relevant to HyECHO.

card.one_liner: KABURI-TTS enables controllable, human-like overlapping speech in two-party dialogues using phoneme-keyed activity conditioning.
card.key_idea: A bi-channel TTS model using a Rectified-Flow DiT backbone, conditioned on per-speaker phoneme rasters and explicit voice activity states to render separate audio channels.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via human subjective ratings (Likert scale) and voice activity analysis on Japanese dialogue data, comparing against Irodori and MOSS-TTSD baselines.
card.limitation: Requires an external module (statistical placement or duration predictor) to construct the phoneme raster from raw text.

slides.title: Development of a Humanoid Robot Prototype for Multimodal Human-Robot Interaction
slides.highlight: This humanoid prototype integrates gesture recognition, object detection, and LLM-based voice processing, providing a testbed for AI-mediated embodied learning relevant to RwB.

card.one_liner: A low-cost, 3D-printed humanoid robot prototype for multimodal human-robot interaction using AI-driven perception.
card.key_idea: Integrates a 12-DOF dual-arm system with MediaPipe/LSTM gesture recognition, YOLO-based 3D object localization, and LLM-based semantic parsing for voice commands via a Jetson AGX Xavier.
card.evaluation: Validated via pick-and-place tasks and social interactions; achieved 96% gesture accuracy, 92% speech accuracy, and average positioning error of 1.83 cm.
card.limitation: Reliance on external LLM APIs introduces latency and dependency on stable internet connectivity.

slides.title: Emotion as a Distribution: Joint Valence-Arousal Probability Learning for Speaker-Independent Multimodal Emotion Recognition
slides.tldr: MULTIMODAL EMOTION RECOGNITION VIA VALENCE-AROUSAL PROBABILITY DISTRIBUTIONS
slides.highlight: This work proposes a text and speech system that outputs a probability matrix over the Valence-Arousal plane, contributing to HyECHO's goals of multimodal social perception and engagement modeling.

card.one_liner: A multimodal emotion recognizer that predicts a joint Valence-Arousal probability distribution instead of a single label.
card.key_idea: A dual-head system using a 9x9 probability matrix trained with 2D-Gaussian soft targets and KL divergence, utilizing Mamba or Transformer temporal backbones.
card.evaluation: Strict speaker-independent 5-fold LOSO on IEMOCAP; mamba_dual_head achieved 73.0% UA, outperforming the Transformer baseline by 3.0 UA points.
card.limitation: State-space backbones showed no latency or memory advantage over Transformers at the studied utterance lengths.

slides.title: Xiaomi Unveils Humanoid Robot 'CyberOne' at IFA 2026
slides.highlight: The unveiling of the CyberOne humanoid robot is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots.

slides.title: Accountable AI with Grounded, Faithful, Consistent, Actionable Rationales: A Case Study in Clinical Trial Matching with VERDICT
slides.tldr: NEUROSYMBOLIC AGENT FOR ACCOUNTABLE AI DECISIONS
slides.highlight: The paper introduces VERDICT, an LLM-based agent that uses SMT solvers to ensure policy consistency and accountability, supporting MIMIC's use of neuro-symbolic agent models for societal-scale impact analysis.

card.one_liner: Verdict ensures accountable clinical trial matching by separating LLM language parsing from SMT-based decision execution.
card.key_idea: Translates trial constraints and patient evidence into SMT/MaxSMT formulas to derive consistent decisions, explicit assumptions, and pivotal conditions (minimal changes to reverse the outcome).
card.evaluation: Tested on SIGIR 2016-derived and TREC 2021 datasets against LLM and neuro-symbolic baselines; achieved highest F1 and clinician-preferred rationales.
card.limitation: Accountability depends on the LLM's accuracy in translating natural language into the formal SMT representation.
